newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian says son died of settler beating.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian says son died of settler beating.

text.p: A 10-year-old Palestinian boy died in hospital on Monday a day after a West bank Jewish settler beat him unconscious on suspicion of stone- throwing, a witness and the boy's family said.
Family members in Husan village, near Bethlehem, wept in grief as news that Hilmi Shosha died from injuries he sustained in the attack on Sunday while returning home from school.
Israel radio said an autopsy performed in Tel Aviv showed that the boy died from a brain haemorrhage caused by a sharp blow to the neck.
Police told Israel Radio that Nahum Kurman, security chief of the settlement of Efrat, was being held for questioning.
Hilmi's father and witnesses said the security chief landed one blow to the boy's head with the handle of his pistol and stomped on him.
"He was beaten by a settler. The boy was in a coma after he was hit and he died in hospital," said Salim Shosha, Hilmi's father at a wake in the village. "He had a haemorrhage in the head."
"A speeding jeep came up and stopped near us. One man got out and hit my cousin," Ibrahim, a classmate of Hilmi who witnessed the incident told Reuters.
"He stomped on him and hit him with the pistol on his head," the boy said, pointing to his head.
The incident highlighted Arab-Jewish tension since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was elected in May on a platform that opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace.
Palestinians at the wake heaped scorn on the Israeli government, accusing it of letting settlers run amock.
A police spokesman told Israel Radio on Sunday that Hilmi collapsed while being chased by Kurman and that there was no proof the settler caused the boy's death.
"I don't believe he caused the death of the boy...I understood he never touched him, that he chased him and the boy fell," said Yoram Kadosh, an official from the nearby Hadar Beitar settlement.
The boy's father denied his son had thrown stones at Israeli cars.
"The man who beat him said himself to my older son -- he did not know it was my son -- that he hit him and had no idea he would fall like that," Shosha told Israel Radio.
Hilmi's relatives said the settler left the boy bleeding for 30 minutes before an ambulance took him to a Jerusalem hospital where he died the next morning.
Around 130,000 Jewish settlers live among two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war.

Israel gave Palestinians limited control over parts of the West Bank after it signed a breakthrough peace agreement with the PLO in 1993 but settlements remain under Israeli control pending a final peace accord.
